text: A real web browser in a terminal pane. kb drives headless Chrome and draws each page as pixels with the kitty graphics protocol , so you see the actual layout, fonts and images, not a text approximation, and you can click, scroll, type, find, zoom and copy in it. It is built for working beside a coding agent. The agent opens kb in the pane next to its own, and you both look at the same page while it loads your dev server, checks for console errors, clicks through a flow, tries a phone width, or reads documentation, all through kb ctl . kb http://localhost:3000 # open a page in this pane kb ctl check # from another pane: is the page healthy? kb skill install # teach Claude Code (or any agent with skills) to use it Status: early but usable, version 0.1. Used daily on macOS in Rex and Ghostty; it should work in kitty and WezTerm, and it builds on Linux, but those haven't been tested yet. Reports are welcome, and if kb is useful to you, a star helps other people find it. With Rust and Chrome installed: cargo install --git https://github.com/graiz/kittybrowser kb news.ycombinator.com Ctrl+/ shows the keys, Ctrl+Q quits. brew install --cask google-chrome # if you don't have Chrome cargo install --git https://github.com/graiz/kittybrowser # puts kb in ~/.cargo/bin kb https://example.com On a non-retina display, start it with kb --scale 1 . Install Chrome or Chromium from your distribution or google.com/chrome, then: cargo install --git https://github.com/graiz/kittybrowser kb --scale 2 https://example.com # --scale 2 on a HiDPI screen; the default is 1 kb looks for google-chrome , google-chrome-stable , chromium , chromium-browser , microsoft-edge and brave-browser on your PATH ; set KB_CHROME=/path/to/browser for anything else. Linux builds cleanly but is untested, so please open an issue with what you find. git clone https://github.com/graiz/kittybrowser cd kittybrowser cargo install --path . Windows kb doesn't run natively on Windows: it needs a Unix terminal and Unix sockets. Use it inside WSL 2 with Chrome or Chromium installed on the Linux side, from a terminal with the kitty graphics protocol (WezTerm runs on Windows). This is untested. Run the same cargo install again (add --force if it says kb is already installed). If you use the agent skill, run kb skill install afterwards so it matches the new version. kb skill remove # if you installed the agent skill kb mcp off # if you turned on the MCP server cargo uninstall kittybrowser rm -rf ~ /.kittybrowser # history, profiles and cookies Using kb kb # start with the address field focused kb example.com # open a page kb rust traits # anything that isn't an address is a web search kb ./page.html # a local file The top row holds back, forward and reload buttons and the address field; the page fills the rest of the pane. The mouse works on both: click the buttons, click the address to edit it, and click, drag and scroll the page. Every other key goes to the page. The mouse's back and forward buttons go back and forward. kb keys lists the bindings; change them in ~/.kittybrowser/keys , one per line ( ctrl+shift+i devtools , or alt+left none to let the page have a key), and running kbs pick up the change at once. kb skill install # installs the skill to ~/.claude/skills/kb The skill teaches an agent (Claude Code, or any agent that reads skills) to open kb in a pane beside its own, find which kb is its own, and work in it while you watch. Its text is skill/SKILL.md ; kb skill show prints it. Any program can drive a running kb with kb ctl : kb ctl open http://localhost:3000 # waits for the load, reports errors kb ctl check # exit 1 on console errors, failed requests or an error page kb ctl click ' text=Save ' # reports the errors and dialogs it causes kb ctl screenshot --out page.png kb ctl viewport 375x800 # a phone width; viewport reset to undo kb ctl outline # read a page: headings, then... kb ctl text --section Installation # ...just one section kb ctl --help lists every command and kb ctl <command> --help describes one: Selectors are CSS (reaching into shadow DOM), text=Some words , @N from kb ctl links , or :focus . With several kbs running, pick one with kb ctl -i N . The same commands are available as an MCP server, which is off until you turn it on: kb mcp on (it prints how to register it with Claude Code), kb mcp off , kb mcp status . Security: kb listens on a socket in ~/.kittybrowser that only your user can open. Anything running as you can use it to run JavaScript in pages you are logged in to in kb. Such a program could already read your files, but it's worth knowing before you turn on the MCP server. See SECURITY.md . MIT. See LICENSE .
